A shift of speed marked in the score, such as Largo to Moderato, that signals a new section.
A change of time signature or beat grouping, which alters how the pulse is felt.
A short passage written to connect two sections: no new theme, only the harmony and motion that lead from one to the other.
A passage for the soloist alone in a concerto or aria, displaying technique over a pause on the dominant; originally improvised.
Italian “attack”: an instruction to go straight on to the next movement without a pause.
An ending in which the music tapers away to nothing instead of closing on a final cadence.
